documentation: zip produces tuples containing one item from each iterable. By default it stops when the shortest iterable is exhausted. strict=True can instead reject unequal lengths.
inputs: Two or more iterables; an optional strict flag.
returns: An iterator of paired or grouped tuples.
caution: The default silently stops at the shortest input. Choose strict=True when unequal lengths indicate a data error.
scenarios: Pair product codes with quantities from a known export.
Compare corresponding values from two time periods.
Combine parallel lists before building structured records.
title: Pair stock codes and quantities
problem: Input has codes (strings) and quantities (integers). Return objects with code and quantity, pairing values by position and stopping at the shorter list.
goal: Use zip() or an equivalent approach that demonstrates the same concept.
hint: Zip the two lists and construct a dictionary for each pair.
